newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: At least four killed in bloody Bogota prison riot.
newsitem.headline: At least four killed in bloody Bogota prison riot.

text.p: At least four inmates were killed and 21 injured in a riot early on Thursday at Bogota's Modelo prison, authorities said.

"The official version, unfortunately, is that there are four dead and 21 injured," Rafael Lamo, head of the National Prisons Institute, told reporters. He added that eight of the injured were in serious condition and were taken to hospitals.

Lamo did not specify the causes of the deaths or injuries. But an aide said the uprising at the ageing prison facility erupted shortly before midnight on Wednesday when rebellious inmates stormed a sentry post and seized a guard's rifle.
Guards moved to put down the riot about two hours later, the prison official said, adding that some of the victims were believed to have been killed or injured by fellow inmates and not guards.

"We believe there was fighting among the inmates themselves," he said, noting that some of the injured had suffered knife wounds and not injuries from the gunshots or tear gas canisters fired by guards.

The riot prompted the government to declare a de facto state of emergency in prisons across the country, which have been rocked by at least a dozen major uprisings against overcrowding and poor livings conditions so far this year.

Lamo said emergency measures would include curbs on visiting rights and government officials said they would make an effort to reduce overcrowding in the Modelo and other prisons by transferring inmates to less crowded facilties.
The Modelo was built to house no more than 1,900 inmates but its current population exceeds 4,500, according to the Prisons Institute.

Officials denied radio reports, based on telephone interviews with inmates of the Modelo, that as many as nine prisoners were gunned down indiscriminately when guards moved to put down what they described as "a peaceful protest."
